key_effect_directions.claim: Accuracy vs S will be fit at least as well by a smooth monotone spline as by a piecewise regime model (piecewise AIC advantage < 10) on at least one of the two task families
The unlimited shared-log baseline will match or exceed the best bounded-S configuration in accuracy on at least one task family
The random-salience control will produce accuracy-vs-S curves statistically indistinguishable from self-assessed salience curves at most S values

forecast.rationale: With three 7B models and 200 items per configuration, accuracy curves will be noisy and most likely saturate smoothly with S; 7B self-assessed salience is weak, so top-S competition rarely beats an unlimited log, and the PASS condition requires both a strong AIC>=10 regime signal on two families and the bottleneck strictly beating unlimited sharing, a conjunction that is a priori unlikely. If apparent breakpoints do appear, they will likely fall at different S across multi-hop QA and constraint puzzles (different information demands), triggering KILL. SPLIT is possible only if one family shows a clean regime and the other does not, which the frozen text arguably folds into FAIL/KILL, so it gets low mass.
